sourcedFrom: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 (2024 — from rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46)
cleanIntro: This guide comes from Laugo's own book for the Alien Remus. The Remus does not strip like the plain Alien, so read this first. The barrel is fixed to the frame and never comes out. The top rail carries the sights and stays still when you fire. On the Remus, a latch lever holds the rail on. You press and hold that lever while you push the rail forward. The recoil assembly also comes out on its own after the slide, not with it. The Remus has a manual safety too. The book says to apply it only with the hammer cocked. The hammer stays cocked the whole time the gun is apart.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber empty — look and feel
steps.action: Point the muzzle somewhere safe. Press the magazine catch and take the magazine out. Pull the slide fully to the rear and look into the chamber. Put a finger in it as well, because a cartridge can hide in a dark port. Leave the safety alone for now. The book says never to put it on with the hammer down. Nothing after this step is safe with a round in the gun.
steps.quote: Ensure the pistol is unloaded by pulling the slide to its rearmost position, and visually confirm that no ammunition is present in the chamber.
steps.cite: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 — Section 5, Stripping and Assembly, p.12
steps.warn: Never engage the safety with the hammer decocked!

steps.title: Rack it once — the cocking indicator must stick out
steps.action: Pull the slide all the way back and let it go. This cocks the hammer. Then look at the back of the pistol. The cocking indicator should now stick out of the rear. If it does not, rack the slide again. Laugo says the slide has to be worked to cock the hammer, and the rail cannot come off until it is cocked. The hammer stays cocked from here until the gun is back together.
steps.quote: Pull the slide to its rearmost position and release it, ensuring that the cocking indicator is now protruding from the rear of your Alien.
steps.cite: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 — Section 5, Stripping and Assembly, p.12

steps.title: Press the marked front area of the rail
steps.action: Find the marked area at the front of the top rail. Press it with your thumb or palm. This frees the latch for the next step. Nothing comes off yet. You are only releasing the latch so the lever at the back can move.
steps.quote: Press the marked front area of the rail with your thumb or palm.
steps.cite: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 — Section 5, Stripping and Assembly, p.12

steps.title: Hold the latch lever down
steps.action: Press the latch lever with the thumb of your weak hand, in the direction of its arrow. Keep holding it. If you let go now, the rail locks again and will not move in the next step.
steps.quote: Use the thumb of your weak hand to press and hold the latch lever in the direction of the arrow.
steps.cite: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 — Section 5, Stripping and Assembly, p.12

steps.title: Push the rear of the rail forward, hard
steps.action: Keep the latch lever pressed. With the same thumb, push the back of the rail firmly forward, toward the muzzle. It takes a firm push and it lets go all at once. Keep your other hand around the gun so the rail does not jump free.
steps.quote: While keeping the latch lever pressed, use your weak hand's thumb to firmly push the rear part of the rail forward in the direction of the shot.
steps.cite: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 — Section 5, Stripping and Assembly, p.12

steps.title: Rail off the pistol
steps.action: Lift the rail off the pistol. It comes off whole, sights and optic mount together. Set it down sights-up so you do not knock the sight adjustment or an optic you have fitted.
steps.quote: Remove the rail from the pistol.
steps.cite: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 — Section 5, Stripping and Assembly, p.14

steps.title: Slide back about 15 mm, up, then off
steps.action: Pull the slide back about 15 mm and lift it. Then lift the back of the slide further and take it off the frame. On the Remus the recoil assembly stays in the frame. Do not pull at the spring to bring it along.
steps.quote: Lift the rear part of the slide further and remove the slide from the frame.
steps.cite: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 — Section 5, Stripping and Assembly, p.14

steps.title: Recoil assembly: forward, lift the front, out
steps.action: Push the recoil assembly forward. Lift its front connector slightly, then take the whole assembly out of the pistol. It comes out in one piece. The front connector is where it hooks, so lift there and not at the spring. This is the step the plain Alien does not have.
steps.quote: Push the recoil assembly to the forward position, slightly lift the front connector of the recoil assembly, and remove it from the pistol.
steps.cite: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 — Section 5, Stripping and Assembly, p.14

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You now have the frame with its fixed barrel, the top rail, the slide, the recoil assembly, and the magazine. Laugo says disassembly is complete here. Stop. The hammer is exposed now. The warning on the same page is to never release it by pressing the sear, because that damages the gun. Leave the hammer cocked for cleaning and for reassembly.
steps.quote: The disassembly of the pistol is complete.
steps.cite: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 — Section 5, Stripping and Assembly, p.14
steps.warn: Never release the hammer by manually manipulating or pressing the sear.

deepSteps.title: The piston chamber
deepSteps.action: Laugo says the piston system needs regular cleaning. A lot of shooting builds up residue in the piston chamber and on the piston. Put Laugo's Carbon Remover on the piston and the piston chamber, and leave it about ten minutes. Then scrub the chamber in a circle with the L-shaped cleaner from the accessories. Brush the piston clean. The book allows metal tools only for buildup a brush will not shift.
deepSteps.quote: Use the manufacturer-supplied Carbon Remover on the piston and piston chamber surfaces.
deepSteps.cite: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 — Section 7, Cleaning and Maintenance — Piston System Cleaning, p.31

deepSteps.title: Recoil spring off the rod, spring base out
deepSteps.action: This is the book's own recoil spring service. Pull the recoil spring away from its clip and unhook it from the recoil spring rod. Then take off the spring and the spring base. Fit the new spring base securely. Slide the spring back onto the rod, pull it to make room, and hook the rod back onto the clip. Laugo says to do a function check afterwards.
deepSteps.quote: Pull the recoil spring away from the clip (Part No. B30) and unhook it from the recoil spring rod.
deepSteps.cite: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 — Section 7, Cleaning and Maintenance — Replacement Steps, p.32

deepSteps.title: Spring base every 10,000 shots
deepSteps.action: The spring base is a scheduled wear part. Laugo puts three spares in the box and says to replace it every 10,000 shots. Keep a count of rounds fired so you know when it is due. Use the step above to change it.
deepSteps.quote: To maintain optimal performance and reliability, replace the Spring Base (Part No. B34) every 10,000 shots.
deepSteps.cite: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 — Section 7, Cleaning and Maintenance — Service Plan, p.32

deepSteps.title: Magazine: slide the base pad L back
deepSteps.action: The magazine comes apart without tools. Slide the base pad L back to its disassembly position, then push the baseplate forward a little. Keep the base of the magazine pointed away from your face, because the spring is still pushing on the baseplate.
deepSteps.quote: Move the base pad L (E04) to the disassembly position and then slightly push the baseplate forward.
deepSteps.cite: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 — Section 5, Stripping and Assembly — Stripping the Magazine, p.17

deepSteps.title: Thumb over the baseplate, then take it off
deepSteps.action: Keep your thumb over the baseplate to hold the spring in. With your other hand, take the baseplate off. Then let the spring come up slowly under your thumb. Laugo says to wear safety glasses for this. The spring is what can hurt you here.
deepSteps.quote: Then place your thumb above the baseplate to secure the spring and with your other hand, remove the baseplate completely.
deepSteps.cite: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 — Section 5, Stripping and Assembly — Stripping the Magazine, p.17
deepSteps.warn: Wearing safety glasses is highly recommended.

deepSteps.title: No further — Laugo stops here
deepSteps.action: The book stops here. It covers only the field strip, the recoil spring base and the magazine. If the gun needs adjusting or repairing, Laugo sends you to a certified workshop or an official service center. The trigger parts, the hammer and the frame parts are not for the owner to take apart.
deepSteps.quote: Do not disassemble any parts of the pistol other than those specifically addressed in this manual.
deepSteps.cite: ALIEN REMUS Instruction Manual (First Edition) — FIRST EDITION, rev. 12/2024 — FIRST EDITION printed on the cover, rev. 12/2024 printed on printed p.46 — Section 5, Stripping and Assembly — Stripping the Magazine, p.17

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: The barrel is fixed, so clean from the chamber end with the pistol stripped
If the gun is new or lightly fired, push a dry cloth on a rod through, or use a bore snake, until it comes out clean
If the bore is heavily soiled, brush a little cleaning fluid into the bore and chamber, leave it about 10 minutes, then brush
Dry the bore and chamber with a clean cloth and check that all residue is gone. Repeat if needed
Push the brush through the full length of the barrel before you change direction, or it can stick

cleaning.name: PISTON SYSTEM
tasks: Carbon Remover on the piston and piston chamber, left about 10 minutes
The L-shaped cleaner from the accessories, turned in a circle around the piston chamber
Brush the piston clean. Use metal tools only for stubborn buildup

cleaning.name: RECOIL ASSEMBLY
tasks: Wipe the recoil assembly clean while it is out of the pistol
Replace the spring base every 10,000 shots. Three spares come in the box
Keep a record of rounds fired so the change is on time

cleaning.name: PRESERVATION
tasks: After cleaning, wipe every part with a cloth lightly damp with preservation oil, or use a light coat of spray oil
Wipe off the extra oil so it does not build up
Run a clean cloth through the bore so it is dry before you shoot
In the cold, remove the oil or use a cold-weather lubricant
Use preservation grease only for long storage in harsh conditions, and clean it all off before use

reassembly: Check the hammer is still cocked. It must be cocked for reassembly as well as disassembly.
Put the recoil spring assembly back in.
Hook the slide onto the recoil spring assembly, then pull it slightly back and down into place.
Set the top rail onto the slide with the hammer cocked. The front of the rail should sit about 3 mm ahead of the front of the slide.
Hold the rail pressed against the pistol and push it into its rearmost position until it clicks and lines up with the front locking hole.
Check the latch lever. A correctly fitted rail has the latch lever in the upper position.
Look at the takedown button and make sure it shows the OK position.
Magazine: the stripping steps in reverse. Hold the spring down under your thumb and slide the baseplate back on until the base pad L locks.
fncheck: First make sure the pistol and the magazine are empty, and point the muzzle somewhere safe. Check that the latch lever is in the upper position and the takedown button shows OK. Pull the slide back and let it go a few times. It should run smoothly and return fully forward, and the rail should not move. With the hammer cocked, move the safety to ON and then OFF. Put it on only with the hammer cocked. Insert the empty magazine and make sure the catch holds it, then press the catch and check the magazine drops free. Finish the way Laugo's unload steps finish: safety off and gun empty, then press the trigger once.
